metadata.title: Implement Service Worker for Asset Caching

story.iWant: the app to load quickly on repeat visits
story.soThat: I get instant access to the interface
story.tasks:
- [ ] Task 1: Research and decide on service worker implementation approach (AC: Service worker registration succeeds) - [ ] Evaluate Next.js 15+ native service worker support capabilities - [ ] Evaluate next-pwa plugin as alternative approach - [ ] Review tech spec recommendation (QUESTION-1: Use next-pwa Plugin or Native Next.js PWA Features?) - [ ] Make decision based on Next.js 15 PWA capabilities and project requirements - [ ] Document chosen approach in Dev Notes with rationale
- [ ] Task 2: Install and configure service worker solution (AC: Service worker registration succeeds) - [ ] If using next-pwa: Install next-pwa package (`npm install next-pwa`) - [ ] If using native: Set up service worker file structure - [ ] Configure next.config.js with service worker settings - [ ] Set disable: true for development mode (production only) - [ ] Configure dest: 'public' for service worker output location - [ ] Enable register: true for automatic service worker registration - [ ] Enable skipWaiting: true for immediate updates (per tech spec QUESTION-5)
- [ ] Task 3: Configure caching strategy for static assets (AC: Static assets cached on first visit, served on subsequent visits) - [ ] Implement cache-first strategy for static JavaScript bundles (/_next/static/.*) - [ ] Implement cache-first strategy for static CSS files (/_next/static/.*) - [ ] Implement cache-first strategy for fonts (if custom fonts loaded) - [ ] Implement cache-first strategy for images (*.png, *.jpg, *.svg, *.webp) - [ ] Set appropriate cache expiration (maxAgeSeconds: 365 days for static, 30 days for images) - [ ] Set maxEntries limits (100 for static-cache, 50 for image-cache) - [ ] Name caches appropriately (static-cache-v1, image-cache-v1)
- [ ] Task 4: Configure network-only strategy for API routes (AC: API calls not cached) - [ ] Implement network-only handler for /api/check-rain route - [ ] Implement network-only handler for all /api/* routes - [ ] Ensure no caching of API responses (fresh data required per ADR-002) - [ ] Verify weather data never stored in service worker cache - [ ] Test API calls bypass service worker cache
- [ ] Task 5: Implement offline fallback behavior (AC: Offline fallback works) - [ ] Configure fallback for offline mode (show cached interface) - [ ] Ensure API calls fail gracefully when offline (return network error) - [ ] Do not implement offline data storage (stateless architecture per ADR-002) - [ ] Display appropriate error message when API unavailable offline - [ ] Test offline mode shows cached UI but requires network for searches
- [ ] Task 6: Test service worker registration and lifecycle (AC: Service worker registration succeeds, updates work) - [ ] Build production version of app (`npm run build`) - [ ] Start production server (`npm run start`) - [ ] Verify service worker registers in Chrome DevTools → Application → Service Workers - [ ] Check service worker status shows "activated and running" - [ ] Verify no registration errors in console - [ ] Test service worker install and activate lifecycle events - [ ] Verify service worker updates when new version deployed (skipWaiting behavior)
- [ ] Task 7: Validate caching behavior (AC: Static assets cached and served from cache) - [ ] Open Chrome DevTools → Application → Cache Storage - [ ] Verify static-cache contains JavaScript and CSS files from /_next/static/ - [ ] Verify image-cache contains icon files from /icons/ - [ ] Test first visit: Assets loaded from network, then cached - [ ] Test second visit: Assets served from cache (instant load) - [ ] Verify cache hit in Network tab (shows "from ServiceWorker" or cache indicator) - [ ] Verify API routes show network requests (not cached)
- [ ] Task 8: Cross-browser service worker testing (AC: Service worker works across browsers) - [ ] Test service worker registration in Chrome (full support) - [ ] Test service worker registration in Edge (full support) - [ ] Test service worker in Safari (limited support, verify graceful degradation) - [ ] Test service worker in Firefox (basic support) - [ ] Verify app works even if service worker fails to register (graceful degradation) - [ ] Document browser-specific limitations in Dev Notes

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: **Given** the app should cache static assets for performance **When** the service worker is implemented **Then** static assets (JS, CSS, fonts) are cached on first visit **And** cached assets are served on subsequent visits **And** service worker updates when new version is deployed **And** network requests for API calls are not cached (online-only) **And** service worker registration succeeds without errors **And** fallback behavior works when offline (show appropriate message)

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Universal Access (PWA)
doc.section: Data Models and Contracts - Service Worker Configuration
doc.snippet: Service worker configuration using next-pwa plugin with cache-first strategy for static assets (lines 132-171). Configuration includes dest: 'public', register: true, skipWaiting: true, disable in development. Runtime caching strategies: CacheFirst for images and static assets, NetworkOnly for API routes.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Universal Access (PWA)
doc.section: Workflows and Sequencing - Service Worker Caching Workflow
doc.snippet: Service worker lifecycle: First visit installs and pre-caches critical assets (/_next/static/css/*.css, /_next/static/js/*.js, /icons/*.png). Subsequent visits serve from cache (cache-first) for static assets, network-only for API calls. Cache storage uses 'static-cache-v1' naming convention (lines 379-428).

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Universal Access (PWA)
doc.snippet: External dependency: next-pwa (latest) for service worker generation and caching. Alternative: @next/pwa official plugin. Note: Next.js 15+ has native PWA support via manifest.ts, but next-pwa may still be required for service worker. Configuration in next.config.js (lines 580-615).

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Universal Access (PWA)
doc.snippet: QUESTION-1: Use next-pwa plugin or Next.js 15+ native PWA features? Research during Story 4.2 implementation. QUESTION-5: RESOLVED - Use skipWaiting: true for immediate service worker updates (simple app, no breaking changes expected) (lines 802-835).

doc.title: Architecture - PWA Support and Stateless Architecture
doc.snippet: Stateless architecture requirement: Service worker caches static assets only, never weather data. No offline data storage (localStorage, IndexedDB). Fresh data required on every API request. Service worker should use network-only strategy for all /api/* routes.

doc.title: Architecture - Technology Stack
doc.snippet: PWA Support: Native Next.js manifest.ts (Next.js 16). No external dependencies for manifest. Service worker implementation may require next-pwa plugin or custom implementation (to be determined in Story 4.2).

constraint.rule: Service worker must NEVER cache API responses. Use network-only strategy for all /api/* routes. No offline data storage (localStorage, IndexedDB). Fresh weather data required on every request.

Service worker must integrate with Next.js 16 build process. Configuration in next.config.js. No breaking changes to existing App Router structure. Service worker enhances but does not require changes to app/page.tsx or app/layout.tsx.

constraint.source: Tech Spec Epic 4 - Service Worker Strategy
constraint.rule: Cache-first strategy for static assets: /_next/static/* (JS, CSS), /icons/* (images), fonts. Network-only strategy for /api/* routes. Service worker disabled in development (production only). Use skipWaiting: true for immediate updates.

Cache naming: static-cache-v1, image-cache-v1. Expiration: maxAgeSeconds 365 days for static, 30 days for images. Max entries: 100 for static-cache, 50 for image-cache. Output location: dest: 'public'.

DO NOT modify app/manifest.ts, app/layout.tsx metadata, or public/icons/* files. These were completed and validated in Story 4.1. Service worker configuration should be additive only (next.config.js changes).
DO NOT modify lib/api-client.ts or app/api/check-rain/route.ts. Service worker must use network-only strategy to ensure API client always fetches fresh data. No breaking changes to API integration.

Service worker must work on Chrome/Edge (full support), Safari (limited support with graceful degradation), Firefox (basic support). App must function normally if service worker fails to register (progressive enhancement).

Service worker registration must be non-blocking (async, after page load). Cache storage size target: < 10MB. Repeat visit load time target: < 500ms (cached assets). Cache hit rate target: 100% for static assets on repeat visits.

tests.standards: Testing standards for service worker implementation: Manual testing required (no automated test suite configured per Story 4.1 notes). Test service worker registration in Chrome DevTools → Application → Service Workers. Verify cache behavior in DevTools → Application → Cache Storage. Test offline mode using DevTools → Network → Offline. Cross-browser testing on Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox. Production build required for service worker testing (disabled in development). Lighthouse PWA audit for installability verification. Test graceful degradation (app works without service worker). Verify no breaking changes to API integration from Story 3.9.

Go offline (DevTools → Network → Offline), refresh page, verify cached interface loads (UI shows), submit search, verify API call fails gracefully with network error message, verify no stale data shown

Test service worker registration in Chrome (full support), Edge (full support), Safari (limited - verify graceful degradation), Firefox (basic support), verify app works even if service worker fails to register

Verify API integration still works (lib/api-client.ts checkRain() function), verify manifest still serves at /manifest.webmanifest, verify icon files accessible, run type-check (npm run type-check) for TypeScript errors
